From A Very Simple Example of the Incompetence of Reporting on Marijuana Prohibition

“However, as President Trump has suggested that he is thinking about discussing considering perhaps revisiting and/or reviewing the possibility of somehow changing the regulatory status of marijuana, being listed in Schedule One, the reporting on it has been demonstrably incompetent. First, the simple facts. So how and why did marijuana get in Schedule One.

 

In 1971, President Nixon’s Attorney General, John Mitchell, who actually went to prison for his role in the Watergate scandal, put marijuana in Schedule One. This was not done one the basis of any scientific study. On the contrary. At about this time, Nixon also created a commission to study marijuana, The Schafer Commission.

 

From the Wikipedia article: “While the Controlled Substances Act was being drafted in a House committee in 1970, Assistant Secretary of Health Roger O. Egeberghad recommended that marijuana temporarily be placed in Schedule I, the most restrictive category of drugs, pending the Commission's report.

 

On March 22, 1972, the Commission's chairman, Raymond P. Shafer, presented a report to Congress and the public entitled "Marihuana: a Signal of Misunderstanding," which favored ending marijuana prohibition and adopting other methods to discourage use.”

 

Of course, Nixon rejected the recommendation of his own commission and simply left marijuana where it was supposed to be only temporarily. Now, over fifty years later it is still there and its status is being treated as though it was one of the Ten Commandments.

What really makes Schedule One different? 

From the DEA: “Schedule I drugs, substances, or chemicals are defined as drugs with no currently accepted medical use and a high potential for abuse.”
